script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination 2026. English Language Paper 3. Listening and Integrated Skills.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The entire broadcast will last approximately one hour. Part A. Task 1. You are at the registration desk for 'The Retail Renaissance Expo'. Listen and complete the form. You have two minutes. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Good morning. Are you here for the Expo? It's wonderful to see so many professionals interested in the future of malls.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Hello, yes. I'm Marcus Yeung. I'm checking in for my team. We are from Global Mall Solutions.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Let me look that up... Global... Global Mall Solutions. Ah, found it. You're the ones doing the big redevelopment in West Kowloon, right?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: That's a different branch. We're the main office based in Central Plaza Tower 2. That's our billing address too, by the way.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Got it. Marcus Yeung, Central Plaza. And your phone number?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: It's 9876 1234. I'm the primary contact for any scheduling changes.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Thank you. Now, your membership status... Oh, wow. You're on the Diamond Executive tier. That gives you first priority for all the breakout sessions.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Yes, we upgraded last month. I have fourteen attendees coming today. I know the original invite said ten, but we brought the whole design department.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Fourteen. Let me adjust the badges... Done. And since you're Diamond, you've been assigned the Grand Atrium Hall for your private consultation. It's much larger than the standard meeting pods.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Perfect. We'll need some tech too. Can we rent those new VR headsets? The ones for the 'Virtual Store' walkthrough?

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: We have a few left. How many do you need? Four?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Actually, three VR headsets should be enough. We can rotate. Also, regarding the lunch—one of our designers is highly allergic to peanuts. So, nut-free only for the catering, please.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Nut-free only. I'll flag that for the chefs. Now, will you be staying for the keynote speaker? It's the CEO of 'Trend-Setters Global'.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Yes, definitely. Wouldn't miss it. What time is the check-in officially recorded?

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: It's 9:15 AM right now. You're early! The workshops don't start until 10:30. Which afternoon session did you pick?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: We're doing the 'Sports Hub Design' session. We were torn between that and 'Gourmet Food Courts', but the sports focus is more urgent for our current project.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: A wise choice. Here are your badges, Marcus. Enjoy the Expo!

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 2. Listen to a presentation about 'Project Playground'. Complete the notes. You have two minutes. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Good morning. My name is Elena Rossi. I'm here to talk about 'Project Playground'. We first brainstormed the concept back in 2022 when we realized that retail alone was no longer a draw for younger crowds. Our pilot mall, 'The Sky-Hub Mall' in East Kowloon, was the first to undergo a total transformation.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Instead of another department store, we installed a massive Indoor Bouldering wall right in the center of the mall. It sounds crazy, but the results were undeniable. In the first quarter alone, we saw a footfall increase of 22%. It wasn't just shoppers; it was people coming to climb and then staying for a smoothie or a coffee. Our primary target demographic is Gen-Z professionals—those who want to fit a workout into their social life.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: The scale is quite significant. We dedicated 10,000 square feet to the sports facilities. While the initial build was expensive, the main recurring cost is the annual insurance, which comes to $1.2 Million due to the high-risk nature of climbing. Our partner for this, the construction firm Apex Build Corp, handled the structural reinforcement perfectly. We are now preparing for a member-only launch on August 15.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Looking forward, we're not stopping at bouldering. Our next project feature is a Digital Skate Park, using motion-tracking sensors. If you have questions, email us at info@project-p.hk. We'll also be hosting a site tour at our Kwun Tong Annex next Friday. Please sign up at the booth.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 3. Listen to three experts discuss the 'Retail-to-Art Shift'. You have two minutes. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Welcome. Dr. Lam, you've studied urban trends for years. Why are malls becoming art galleries?

script.speaker: Dr Lam
script.text: It's simple: online shopping. People buy things on their phones now. Malls have to offer what the internet can't—a physical, emotional experience. Art provides that 'Instagrammable' moment that drives foot traffic.

script.speaker: Ms Gomez
script.text: I agree, but malls often treat art like wallpaper. To do it right, they should hire full-time curators. You wouldn't let a marketing manager run a museum, so why let them run a mall gallery? We need professional storytelling.

script.speaker: Mr Tan
script.text: The cost is the issue for artists. I believe we should have zero admission fees for these mall galleries. If you charge people to enter, they'll just stay in the food court. The mall makes money from the increased coffee and fashion sales, so the art should be a free magnet. We've set a grant application deadline of October 31 for artists who want to participate. We're offering a subsidy cap of $45,000 per artist to cover materials. Currently, we have 25 locations signed up.

script.speaker: Dr Lam
script.text: And the tech is vital. There's a new exhibition app called 'Art-Walk-HK' that guides you through the mall. It's trilingual—Cantonese, English, and Mandarin—which is great for tourists. Most of the pieces are Digital Installations, as they take up less physical space but have high impact. Our lead sponsor, Heritage Bank, has even agreed to keep the commission rate at a low 10% for any art sold. For feedback, please call 2100 3300.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 4. Listen to stakeholders discuss mall sports policies. You have four minutes. (240-second pause)

script.speaker: Tenant A
script.text: I own a high-end boutique. Honestly, the noise from the basketball court next door is too disruptive for retail. My customers expect a quiet, luxury environment. If the mall keeps these sports, my rent should be lowered to compensate for the lost atmosphere. At the very least, they should restrict sports to the roof level, far away from the shops.

script.speaker: Athlete B
script.text: As a coach, I see it differently. The noise creates an energetic atmosphere. It makes the mall feel alive! The rent we pay for the facility is fair given the quality of the equipment. I actually think we should expand to group classes like HIIT or Yoga in the common areas.

script.speaker: Manager C
script.text: We need to balance both. I've looked into acoustic paneling to dampen the sound near the luxury shops. As for rent, we might move to a variable model based on peak hours. But one thing we all agree on is safety—we must have mandatory medical clearance for anyone using the high-intensity zones. We'll also extend operating hours until 11 PM daily to accommodate after-work crowds. We'll have our next review in January 2027.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Part B. Integrated Skills Recording. Listen to the briefing from the Bureau Chief.

script.speaker: Bureau Chief
script.text: Project Manager, we need to move fast on the 'Experience Economy' rollout. For Task 8, when you write to the complaining tenant, don't just mention the rent. Explain that we are offering 'Heritage preservation credits' to shops that integrate art into their storefronts. This is a huge tax break that isn't in the brochure yet. Also, for the internal memo in Task 9, I want you to propose a 'Summer Skate Jam' event in August to boost the footfall gap. It'll be a great way to use the new facility. Finally, for the social media post, use the catchphrase 'Retail Therapy 2.0'. And very importantly, mention that we've installed 'Anti-Slip Flooring' throughout the sports zones to address the safety concerns of the elderly. This is a key safety feature only the board knows about for now. Get to work.

data_file.title: Minutes of the Experience Economy Steering Committee
data_file.content: Date: May 12, 2026. Participants: Sarah Wong (Retail), Leo Chen (Sports Dept). Points: 1. Public approval of mall-based sports is high (68%). 2. However, traditional tenants are complaining about noise. 3. Action: Create a 'Community Ambassador' role to mediate between athletes and shoppers. 4. Goal: Transition 30% of floor space to non-retail by 2028.

data_file.title: The Sky-Hub: More Than a Mall
data_file.content: Features: - 15m Bouldering Wall. - Digital Art Gallery. - 22% increase in foot traffic. - Coming soon: Rooftop Running Track. - Join our 'Active Life' membership for $200/month.

data_file.title: Complaint from Boutique Owner (Mrs. Clara Li)
data_file.content: Subject: Unacceptable Noise Levels. The new 'Sports Zone' is right next to my jewelry shop. The shouting and music are scaring off my VIP clients. I am losing money every day. I want a rent reduction or I am moving out.

data_file.title: Editorial: The End of the Storefront?
data_file.content: SCMP News: Hong Kong malls are evolving. Experts say 'The Experience Economy' is the only way to survive the e-commerce wave. Integrating art and sports isn't just a trend; it's a necessity for survival.

data_file.title: Urgent Note from CEO
data_file.content: To PM: Mrs. Li is influential. We can't lose her shop. Mention the new Curated Window Program. We give them $20,000 to turn their window into an art piece. Also, tell staff we're hiring 50 'Experience Ambassadors' to help with the crowds.

data_file.title: Table: Spending Habits by Mall Zone (Q1 2026)
data_file.content: Zone | Traffic | Avg Spend | Status. Retail | -10% | $800 | Declining. Sports | +22% | $150 | High Volume. Art | +15% | $300 | Growing. Food | +5% | $200 | Stable. Note: The 'Publicity' for the Art zone is currently underfunded.

data_file.title: Viral Post: #SaveOurShops
data_file.content: 1.2k Likes: 'Malls should be for shopping, not for gym rats. I can't even walk through the atrium without getting hit by a basketball. Who is in charge?'

data_file.title: Internal Memo: Experience Ambassador Roles
data_file.content: We are hiring 50 staff to act as 'Experience Ambassadors'. They will manage the flow between the sports zones and retail stores, ensuring noise is kept at reasonable levels and directing traffic.

data_file.title: Insurance Weekly: Mall Liability
data_file.content: Apex Build Corp has secured a new safety certification for mall-based climbing walls. This includes high-impact foam flooring and mandatory harness checks for all participants.

data_file.title: Draft Section: Zoning for Experience
data_file.content: Clause 8.1: No high-decibel activities (e.g., basketball, HIIT) allowed within 20 meters of 'Luxury Tier' retail outlets. Clause 8.2: All art galleries must provide trilingual descriptions.
